data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A corrupted-checklist control within the same evaluation is necessary and sufficient to distinguish genuine rule-mediated reliability from structural or compliance artifacts: if the panel with a corrupted checklist still outperforms the expert, the checklist's rule content is epiphenomenal.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The corrupted checklist accidentally produces correct answers on the discriminating cases, undermining the contrast.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Panel members recognize the corrupted rules as wrong and spontaneously override them, importing external knowledge and contaminating the control.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The corrupted checklist degrades panel morale or engagement, producing a performance difference attributable to motivation rather than rule content.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"There is no feasible way to corrupt the checklist while preserving its procedural structure (e.g., the checklist is too short or too binary to meaningfully corrupt).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The real checklist's advantage over the corrupted one is confined to cases where both are correct, leaving the rule-content contrast unobservable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The confound is checklist-as-procedure versus checklist-as-content. A corrupted-checklist control (wrong rules, preserved format and deliberation structure) isolates the causal contribution of rule content. If the corrupted-checklist panel matches or exceeds the real-checklist panel, the gain is structural or procedural, not epistemic\u2014checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer. If the real-checklist panel outperforms the corrupted-checklist panel specifically on cases where the real rule is correct and the corrupted rule is wrong, the rule content is doing genuine work. This directly tests the speculative concern (SCR_003) that a checklist might improve reliability by structuring deliberation even with wrong rules, which would be a genuine but non-epistemic contribution.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
